         The instant filing is a general rate case; the proposed changes to WBI Energy’s
 rates are supported by the statements and schedules required by section 154.312 of the
 Commission’s regulations, 18 C.F.R. § 154.312. This transmittal letter includes a

2.     eTariff XML Filing Package. The package contains the proposal in electronic

3.     Clean Tariff Sections. As required by 18 C.F.R. § 154.201(a), a PDF file of the
       clean revised tariff records for posting in the Commission’s eLibrary;

4.     Marked Tariff Sections. As required by 18 C.F.R. § 154.201(a), a PDF file of the
       marked revised tariff records for posting in the Commission’s eLibrary;

5.     Accounting Representation. As required by the Commission’s regulations, 18

       representative is included in this filing;

 IV.    NO PENDING FILINGS

        Pursuant to 18 C.F.R. § 154.204(f), which requires a list of other filings pending
with the FERC that may significantly affect the instant filing, WBI Energy states that there
are no other pending filings it is aware of that may affect this filing.

V.     STATEMENT OF NATURE, REASONS AND BASIS

       A.      Introduction

       WBI Energy’s last general rate case was filed on January 27, 2023, in Docket No.
RP23-377-000. Settlement rates in that proceeding took effect on August 1, 2023, pursuant
to an Offer of Settlement and Stipulation and Agreement (“Settlement Agreement”) that
was approved by the Commission on November 27, 2023, WBI Energy Transmission, Inc.,
185 FERC ¶ 61,144 (2023).

        WBI Energy is submitting the instant filing in accordance with that Settlement
Agreement’s Article VII, Comeback and Moratorium Provisions, whereby WBI Energy
agreed it would not file a new Section 4 general rate case before August 1, 2025, but would
make a filing that proposes new rates to be effective, assuming a five-month suspension
period in the instance of a proposed rate increase, no later than August 1, 2028.

        Since its last rate case, WBI Energy has continued to invest in its interstate natural
gas transmission system. WBI Energy has completed several projects since its last rate
case, as reflected in Statement O-2, Exhibit No. WBI-0079 and the increase in rate base.
In addition, costs attributable to pipeline operation and maintenance, labor and associated
expenses, and property taxes have continued to rise. When compared with WBI Energy’s
currently effective rates, the proposed rates in this proceeding are expected to produce an
annual increase in jurisdictional revenues of approximately $31 million.

        WBI Energy continues to face significant market risk and growing competition.
WBI Energy’s system is comprised largely of older, small-diameter pipeline that serves
some of the most sparsely populated markets in the country, and the system is located at
least “one pipeline away” from any major market. Physical constraints on WBI Energy’s
system and high utilization on downstream pipelines create challenges for WBI Energy to
effectively market its transportation and storage services, limiting growth opportunities in
both on-system and off-system markets. The increase in natural gas production from shale
plays near market-demand centers continues to displace the supply basins connected to
WBI Energy’s system. This, coupled with the narrowing of basis differentials due to the
increase in production, further undermines WBI Energy’s ability to market its services,
particularly its off-system transportation services. Revised rates that take these conditions
into consideration will ensure that WBI Energy can earn a just and reasonable rate of return.




                                              4
        B.      Continuation of Postage Stamp Rates for Integrated System and
               Separately Stated Rates for Garden Creek and Stateline Lateral
               Facilities.

        WBI Energy proposes to continue its postage-stamp rate design for most of its
pipeline system, referred to as the “Integrated System,” as it is contiguous and is operated
on an integrated basis.

       WBI Energy also proposes to continue its separately stated transportation rates for
the Garden Creek and Stateline Lateral facilities. Separately stated transportation rates are
appropriate for these facilities because they are not integrated with the rest of WBI
Energy’s system. These facilities cannot access the transmission and storage facilities on
WBI Energy’s Integrated System.

       C.      Incremental Rates for the Valley Expansion, the North Bakken
               Expansion, and the Wahpeton Expansion.

        The continuation of an incremental transportation reservation rate under
WBI Energy’s Rate Schedule FT-1 for the Valley Expansion, which was certificated by
the Commission in Docket No. CP17-257-000, is appropriate as these facilities do not
qualify for rolled-in rate treatment at this time.

        The continuation of an incremental transportation reservation rate under WBI
Energy’s Rate Schedule FT-1 for the North Bakken Expansion, which was certificated by
the commission in Docket Nos. CP20-52-000, et al. is appropriate as these facilities do not
qualify for rolled-in rate treatment at this time.

       WBI Energy is also proposing an incremental transportation reservation rate under
WBI Energy’s Rate Schedule FT-1 for firm transportation service on its Wahpeton
Expansion, placed into service December 1, 2024. The Commission certificated this
expansion in Docket No. CP22-466-000 and approved an incremental reservation rate.
These facilities do not qualify for rolled-in rate treatment at this time.

         WBI Energy calculated a commodity rate for each expansion based on variable
operation and maintenance expense and applicable billing determinants. The resulting
commodity rates were less than WBI Energy’s Integrated System commodity rate proposed
in this rate case. Therefore, due to the integrated nature of the expansions, WBI Energy is
proposing a composite commodity rate for its Integrated System, Valley Expansion, North
Bakken Expansion, and Wahpeton Expansion. The proposed composite commodity rate
is also less than it would otherwise be for the Integrated System. Also, in accordance with
Commission policy, WBI Energy is proposing to use its Integrated System rates under Rate
Schedule IT-1 for any interruptible service made available on the Valley, North Bakken,
and Wahpeton Expansions.




                                             5
        D.      Revised Rates

       The revised rates shown on the tariff records submitted with this filling were
developed as follows:

         1.    Test Period

         The Test Period costs and rate design billing determinants used to calculate the rates
in this filing are based on actual operations for the period ended January 31, 2026, adjusted
for known and measurable changes anticipated to occur during the nine-month period
ending October 31, 2026. The filing reflects an increase in annual jurisdictional revenues
of approximately $31 million compared to the rates currently in effect, as supported by
Statement G of this filing, Exhibit No. WBI-0023.

         2.    Cost of Service

        This filing justifies an overall annual cost-of-service of approximately $268 million
as shown on Statement A, Exhibit No. WBI-0001. The cost of service is supported by the
Prepared Direct Testimonies of WBI Energy witnesses Lori Myerchin, Exhibit No. WBI-
0081, and Becky Heley, Exhibit No. WBI-0083. WBI Energy’s last rate case was settled
on a black box basis. In that proceeding, WBI Energy’s filed cost of service was
approximately $220.3 million.

         3.    Rate Base

       WBI Energy has a net rate base of approximately $931 million as shown on
Statement B, Exhibit No. WBI-0002, inclusive of the Valley Expansion, North Bakken
Expansion, and Wahpeton Expansion and the two non-integrated lateral facilities. WBI
Energy’s proposed rate base in Docket No. RP23-377-000 was approximately $708.3
million.

         4.    Accumulated Deferred Income Tax and Tax Rate

        The computation of the amount of Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes (“ADIT”)
was prepared in accordance with the Commission’s policy of full normalization and the
provision for ADIT represents full recognition of book to tax timing differences and
Internal Revenue Service regulations.

        The calculation of ADIT for WBI Energy is supported by the Prepared Direct
Testimony of WBI Energy witness Myerchin, Exhibit No. WBI-0081, and Schedule B-1,
Exhibit No. WBI-0003. WBI Energy has reflected, as a direct reduction to the cost of
service, a flowback amount associated with the excess ADIT balance reflected in the
Settlement Agreement from WBI Energy’s rate case in Docket No. RP19-165-000,
resulting from the reduction in the federal corporate income tax rate included in the Tax
Cuts and Job Act of 2017. WBI Energy has also reflected a flowback amount associated
with an excess ADIT balance resulting from a lower combined state income tax rate as


                                              6
 further explained by WBI Energy witness Myerchin, Exhibit No. WBI-0081. The
flowback amounts are provided on Schedule B-1(a), Exhibit No. WBI-0004, and shown on
Statement A and Schedule I-1, Exhibit Nos. WBI-0001 and WBI-0057, respectively.

        Witness Myerchin also supports WBI Energy’s proposed composite federal and
state income tax rate of 24.25%.

             5.    Depreciation and Composite Negative Salvage

       WBI Energy’s proposed depreciation rates and negative salvage rates
(encompassing both interim and terminal retirements) are supported by the Prepared Direct
Testimony of WBI Energy witness Steven R. Fall, Exhibit No. WBI-0104 and Kevin
Lange, Exhibit No. WBI-0109. Witness Fall’s testimony and exhibits are supported by the
Prepared Direct Testimony of WBI Energy witnesses Alexander J. Kirk, Exhibit No. WBI-
0092, who testifies on the appropriate economic life for WBI Energy’s system.

             6.    Overall Return on Capital, Return on Equity, Cost of Debt and Capital
                   Structure

        The revenue requirement reflects an overall rate of return of 11.01% and a return
on equity (“ROE”) of 14.59%. This ROE is supported in the Prepared Direct Testimony
of WBI Energy witness David Haag, Exhibit No. WBI-0085. Witness Haag relied on two
FERC-approved measures for computing ROE: Discounted Cash Flow and the Capital
Asset Pricing Model. WBI Energy reserves the right to make appropriate changes to its
claimed ROE to reflect any changes in capital markets. The proxy group of five comparable
entities used to calculate an ROE for WBI Energy is supported by Witness Haag. Witness
Haag also addresses the business risk faced by WBI Energy, and such business risk is
further detailed in the Prepared Direct Testimony of WBI Energy witness Mark D.
Anderson, Exhibit No. WBI-0082.

        WBI Energy proposes a cost of debt of 4.65%. The cost of debt is set forth on
Schedule F-3, Exhibit Nos. WBI-0021 and WBI-0022, which are sponsored and supported
in the testimony of Witness Myerchin, Exhibit No. WBI-0081.

        WBI Energy proposes to utilize its own capital structure of 36% debt and 64%
equity, which is supported in the testimonies of Witnesses Myerchin, Exhibit No. WBI-
0081, and Haag, Exhibit No. WBI-0085.2

             7.    Discount Adjustment

       WBI Energy is seeking a discount adjustment in the form of a revenue credit to
account for its discounted volumes. Such volumes were discounted to meet competition.
The need for discounting is supported in the testimony of Witness Anderson, Exhibit No.
WBI-0082. Witness Myerchin’s testimony, Exhibit No. WBI-0081, supports
WBI Energy’s proposed discount adjustment and discounting methodology.

           8.     Cost Classification, Allocation, and Rate Design

        WBI Energy continues the use of the straight-fixed variable method for cost
allocation and rate design for transportation rates as directed by the Commission in Order
Nos. 636, et seq.3

        WBI Energy proposes separately stated firm and interruptible transportation rates
for the Garden Creek and Stateline Lateral facilities. As discussed above, these facilities
are non-contiguous and not operationally integrated with the rest of WBI Energy’s system.
The proposed rate treatment for these facilities is supported in the testimony of Witness
Myerchin, Exhibit No. WBI-0081.

        WBI Energy also proposes incremental transportation reservation rates for the
Valley, North Bakken, and Wahpeton Expansions, as discussed above. WBI Energy is
proposing a composite commodity rate for its Integrated System, Valley Expansion, North
Bakken Expansion, and Wahpeton Expansion. WBI Energy is proposing to use its
Integrated System rates under Rate Schedule IT-1 for any interruptible service made
available on the Valley, North Bakken, and Wahpeton Expansions. The proposed rate
treatment for these facilities is supported in the testimony of Witness Myerchin, Exhibit
No. WBI-0081.

          9.     Basis for Proposed Changes

       The basis for WBI Energy’s rate changes is set forth in the statements and schedules
submitted as part of this filing and identified in the attached Exhibit List. WBI Energy has
included in support of its filing all exhibits, statements, schedules, and work papers as
required by 18 C.F.R. § 154.312 of the Commission’s regulations, and as otherwise
necessary to support the revised rates.
